back: Shareholders' responsibility for company debts is limited to the amount they have invested; personal property is protected.
A company is a legal person distinct from its owners: it can own property, make contracts and sue or be sued.
Shares are sold privately and cannot be offered to the general public.
May offer its shares to the general public, usually through a stock exchange.
Owners (shareholders) are different people from those who run the company (directors and managers).
Number of shares held × dividend per share.
Control needs more than 50% of the votes, alone or with allies; the largest holding may not be enough.
Limited liability, easier capital and continuity; but formalities, disclosure, shared profit and possible loss of control.
Gains: large capital, higher profile, easy sale of shares. Costs: loss of control, takeover risk, more disclosure and cost.
